newsitem.title: FINLAND: Albright, Primakov seek to narrow differences.
newsitem.headline: Albright, Primakov seek to narrow differences.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov met for 45 minutes on Thursday in another effort to narrow differences ahead of the Helsinki summit but major issues remain for their two presidents to work out, U.S. officials said.
Primakov, who held three days of talks in Washington last weekend, came back to the Americans with some answers to outstanding questions, one U.S. official told reporters without elaboration.
The two ministers spent most of the time talking about European security, NATO enlargement and arms control, although economics also came up, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

"They tried to determine what they could agree on and what they could kick upstairs" for discussion when U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin have dinner Thursday night and hold day-long talks on Friday, he said.
"Over the last months we've been narrowing differences but there's a lot of work to do and that's what tomorrow is all about," he said.
The official refused to be specific about Thursday's discussion and on what issues there may have been progress.
Albright and Primakov "have been narrowing differences and working on the issues" since Albright was in Moscow three weeks ago, he said.

U.S. officials say the serious work of preparing for the Helsinki summit was during Albright's February visit to Moscow when the two sides laid out areas of agreement and disagreement and Primakov declared that the Russians would "seek to minimise the consequences" of NATO enlargement.
One U.S. official described Friday's summit as a "moment in time" between Albright's Moscow meetings and the July summit in Madrid when NATO plans to invite new members to join the alliance.
Earlier, Albright dismissed tough Russian criticism of NATO enlargement ahead of the summit as insignificant "rhetoric".
Albright spoke as she posed for pictures witht Finnish Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen after arriving in Helsinki.
Asked by reporters about persistent attacks on NATO enlargement plans from Russian officials, Albright said:
"I think we have a lot of work to do...rhetoric leading up to the summit is not what is important. What's important is the discussion that'll take place."
On Wednesday, Russian presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said NATO's planned eastward expansion would be the West's biggest mistake since the end of the Cold War.
